Looking at the documentation and your requirements, I'll create a FigDown topology document for the branch office WAN uplinks.

The key observations from your description:
- **Genre**: `topology` (for network topologies)
- **Nodes**: 5 total (2 access switches, 1 branch router, 2 regional hub routers)
- **Edges**: 4 links as specified (access1→branch, access2→branch, branch→hubprimary, branch→hubbackup)
- **Title**: "Branch office WAN uplinks"

The topology genre is experimental (EXPERIMENTAL), so I'm using standard graph DSL conventions for node and edge declarations. Here's the finished document:

```figdown
# FigDown — figures as text. Spec: https://github.com/FigDown/figdown
figdown 0.1 topology
title "Branch office WAN uplinks"

node access1 "Access Switch 1"
node access2 "Access Switch 2"
node branch "Branch Router"
node hubprimary "Regional Hub (Primary)"
node hubbackup "Regional Hub (Backup)"

edge access1 branch
edge access2 branch
edge branch hubprimary "Primary WAN Link"
edge branch hubbackup "Backup WAN Link"
```

**Structure:**
- The access switches connect locally to the branch router (two local links)
- The branch router then connects to two separate regional hubs via distinct WAN paths — primary and backup for redundancy
- Each node and edge uses the ids you specified and carries human-readable labels describing the device roles and link purposes
